Orange alert in 10 Keralam districts as heavy rain triggers damage
The IMD forecasts thunderstorms accompanied by moderate rainfall as heavy rainfall uproots trees, damages houses
Thiruvananthapuram, Oct 9 (PTI) Heavy rain lashed parts of Keralam on Friday as the IMD issued an orange alert in 10 districts, warning of intense rainfall and thunderstorms, officials said.
The orange alert was issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) in a nowcast bulletin released at 4 pm for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Malappuram, Kozhikode and Kasaragod districts, forecasting intense rainfall over the next three hours.
An orange alert indicates the possibility of heavy rainfall ranging from 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm.
According to a statement issued by the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA), thunderstorms accompanied by moderate rainfall and maximum surface wind speeds of up to 50 kmph were likely at isolated places in these districts.
The IMD also forecast thunderstorms accompanied by moderate rainfall and winds reaching speeds of up to 40 kmph at isolated places in the remaining districts of Keralam, the statement said.
Heavy rain and strong winds uprooted trees in Kollam and Pathanamthitta districts, KSDMA officials said.
Waterlogging was also reported in Aluva in Ernakulam district following the downpour.
Two houses were partially damaged in a thunderstorm and lightning strike in Kannur district, officials added. PTI

Yellow alert returns as Tricity braces for weekend thunderstorms
IMD warns of thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph from Saturday to Monday; day temperatures rise, while nights remain warmer than normal and humidity stays high
After two days of relative relief, temperatures began rising again across Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula on Friday, even as the India Meteorological Department issued a yellow alert for thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds from Saturday to Monday.
The weather department has forecast gusty winds of 40-50 kmph accompanying thunderstorms and lightning on all three days. Scattered rainfall is likely on Sunday, while isolated showers may occur on the other forecast days through Wednesday.
Chandigarh recorded a maximum temperature of 32.3°C on Friday, up 1.1°C from the previous day and 0.2°C above normal. The minimum also rose by 1.2°C to 23.4°C, remaining 4.1°C above normal.
Mohali recorded a maximum of 32.2°C, up 0.9°C from the previous day, while its minimum rose by 1.1°C to 23.8°C. Panchkula recorded a maximum of 30.8°C, up 1.1°C, and a minimum of 22°C, up 1.6°C, to stay coolest in the Tricity.
The rise in both day and night temperatures marks a reversal of the cooling recorded earlier in the week. While daytime readings in Chandigarh and Mohali were close to normal, night temperatures remained appreciably above normal.
Relative humidity remained high in Chandigarh, ranging from 56% to 87%, adding to the muggy conditions. The city recorded no rainfall during the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on Friday or between 8.30 am and 5.30 pm. Its October rainfall total remained 7.8 mm, 29.1% below normal.
The five-day forecast for the Tricity puts maximum temperatures at 30°C on Saturday, 29°C on Sunday, 30°C on Monday, 31°C on Tuesday and 32°C on Wednesday. Minimum temperatures are forecast to fall from 23°C on Saturday to 22°C on Sunday and 21°C from Monday through Wednesday.
The broader forecast indicates isolated rainfall in Punjab and Haryana on Friday and Saturday, with scattered activity likely on Sunday. Isolated showers may continue on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.
Across the region, the average maximum temperature rose by 1.3°C in Haryana and 1.1°C in Punjab on Friday, with both states remaining near normal. Hisar recorded Haryana’s highest maximum at 37.3°C, while Faridkot recorded Punjab’s highest at 38.2°C.
The yellow alert calls for caution over the weekend and on Monday, with thunderstorms, lightning and strong gusty winds expected to accompany the possibility of rain.

THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Heavy rain continues in Kerala, with an orange alert issued for 10 districts over the coming hours. The districts under the orange alert are Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Malappuram, Kozhikode and Kasaragod.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said isolated spells of moderate rain accompanied by thunderstorms and strong winds reaching speeds of up to 50 kmph are likely in these districts.
In the remaining districts, isolated spells of moderate rain accompanied by thunderstorms and strong winds reaching speeds of up to 40 kmph are likely, the IMD said.
